title: Records from the 1950s: Primitive Piano and Jazz Begins
summary: Wood owns Irvin Helfer's Primitive Piano and the Atlantic Young Tuxedo record, and met Wendell Brunious, whose father played trumpet on it.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Okay. I don't have many records, and I don't think that I have but two that I can really identify as going back to the 50s. One is a record that someone named Irvin Helfer produced when he was an undergraduate called Primitive Piano, and he went off and recorded, made tapes of, it must be four or five, maybe six different piano players that he's got on the record. Billy Pierce is one that he's got on there.
Yeah. Some of them he recorded himself, and some of them he got from somebody else, you know, things like that.
But it was an interesting record.

I've still got that. And then there's another record that I have, and I think I must have bought it before I left New Orleans when I was through being in graduate school, and it's this Atlantic recording of the young Tuxedo Brass Band called Jazz Begins. Was that produced in 58, 59, 58? Yeah. Yeah. I've got that, and I have, that's a continuing pleasure to me. I still play that record a lot. And I was intrigued when I was down here last summer to hear a band one afternoon playing down at the gazebo, and when they introduced the members of the band, that one of them was named Wendell Brunius, and so after they were finished playing, I went over and engaged him in conversation and found out that, yes, indeed, he was the son of the man who used to play the trumpet in the young Tuxedo Brass Band, and that I remembered that they had recorded that Atlantic record, part of it at least, at the band playing outside in John Brunius' backyard, and Wendell pointed out to me that his picture is on the album, that the photograph has a little kid in it, and he's the little kid that they took of the bandstand in the backyard. So I thought that was really, it was a nice sort of link and continuity for me, and I enjoyed hearing him play, and since I've been down here this summer, I've enjoyed hearing him play, and I enjoyed him sing. I didn't realize until last Sunday that he also does a lot of vocals, but, and he's been very cordial and very pleasant to me. I think of him as a friend, really. And I bought his record the other night. I took it home. I haven't played it yet, but somebody told me it's really not a bad record,
so I'm glad to have that.
